one_line_contribution: A net-point measurement on ALFWorld that per-item credit for a retrieved memory item is reference-dependent, and that the reference matching what pruning actually does is not the empty slot but the retriever's next-ranked candidate promoted into it, with a test of whether summed single-item credits predict the cost of pruning two items.
closest_prior_work: CUE-R, arxiv:2604.05467 (VERIFIED, s2cli/S2+HF: 2026-04-07, 2 citations). It is already an intervention-based per-evidence-item utility framework whose whole design varies the reference (REMOVE / REPLACE / DUPLICATE) and reports that the intervention type changes the item's measured utility; it also already supplies the evidence-role taxonomy for interpreting those differences. What it does not do is make the replacement the retriever's own next-ranked candidate, tie a reference to a downstream pruning decision, or run in a multi-step agent -- so it does not scoop the specific backfill reference, but it does scoop the framing claim 'per-item utility depends on which counterfactual you use', which is the conceptual half of this proposal. The mechanism half is older and also verified: arxiv:2011.03623 (Feature Removal Is a Unifying Principle for Model Explanation Methods, VERIFIED via s2cli/HF) organizes removal-based explanation exactly around 'how the feature is removed' as the first axis; arxiv:2508.14482 (VERIFIED, 2025-08-20) already argues in so many words that a baseline 'must not merely lack signal, but must represent a plausible state', which is this proposal's entire argument for backfill; arxiv:2607.14271 (VERIFIED, 2026-07-15, Local Additive Feature Attribution: A Mathematical Taxonomy and Reporting Checklist) already names 'reference' as one of five specification choices. The proposal cites the last two itself, which is honest but self-defeating: after those, the remaining contribution is the choice of one particular reference in one particular domain plus a number. I also checked arxiv:2507.04480 (VERIFIED, PKDD/ECML Workshops 2025-07-06, 7 citations, hole-based SHAP over RAG documents) and arxiv:2509.12765 (VERIFIED, InfoGain-RAG, EMNLP, 12 citations, document information gain), which the proposal characterizes correctly. arxiv:2605.01302 (CoRM-RAG) also VERIFIED via search. I could NOT verify 2606.29502 (UCOB), 2605.30712 (ExpSuite), 2606.16285 (HiMPO), 2512.10696 (ReMe), 2607.22562 (SF-AMS), or 2603.05093; 2605.04811 (TreeMem) did return in a search and is verified.
strongest_objection: The headline claim is true by construction and the confirmatory content collapses onto one already-measured quantity. Backfill is DEFINED as what the frozen deterministic retrieval log returns after the item is pruned, so 'only backfill predicts what pruning realizes' cannot fail at the per-game level; the only arm that could break the identity (R1, actually prune the bank and re-retrieve, which couples games through shared items) is explicitly optional, non-confirmatory, and runs only if time remains. Strip the tautology and P3 reduces to P1, and P1 reduces to 'the rank-4 expert item is worth something when added to a 2-item set' -- whose sign the program's own nested-k sweep already reports for free (items 4-7 add +2 to +4 net on top of [1,2,3]; k1->k3, i.e. TWO added items, is only +6.8/+9.3 net). That same prior argues the true g_1 is roughly +3 to +5, and the design's own numbers then make the experiment undecidable: CI +/-5, confirmation at g_1 >= +8, falsification at g_1 <= 0 with the CI excluding +8. The a-priori most likely outcome lands in the (0, +8) dead band and decides nothing, and the same dead-band structure repeats for P3 (0 to +12 at +/-7) and P4. A reviewer will also note that P2's band (-10) is not tied to the program's measured effect -- the wrong-type placebo blind1 was only -3 net against k0 -- which violates the round's own binding rule that margins be stated against measured effects, and that the proposal itself concedes P2 and the class factor 'can say nothing about class x reference interactions', so the second-largest arm block buys nothing for the central claim.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Promote R1 to confirmatory and state a prediction on s(B1) - s(R1): that is the only measurement in the plan that tests, rather than assumes, that the frozen-log backfill equals what bank-level pruning realizes, and it is also where the interesting failure lives (shared items couple games, so per-game backfill can be right while the pruning policy is wrong). Also verify and report that the retriever has no MMR/diversity/dedup step, since rank-order refill equals re-retrieval only for a set-independent scorer. (2) Re-derive the bands from the measured k-curve instead of asserting +8/+12: with a prior of g_1 ~ +3 to +5 the design needs either a pre-registered three-way decision rule that covers the whole line (superiority above a threshold, TOST equivalence inside a margin, indeterminate outside both) or more seeds on fewer games so the rank-1 CI is +/-2 to 3. (3) Replace the class arm (P2), which the proposal admits is definitionally uninformative here, with the decision-level test the title promises: rank items by hole credit and by backfill credit, prune the bottom-m of the bank under each ranking, re-retrieve, and measure realized success. 'The two references disagree about which items to prune, and the hole ranking loses X net points' is a claim worth a paper; 'the two references differ by 8 net points at one slot' is a calibration note. (4) Add the content-free filler control below.
missing_baseline: A token-matched, content-free filler in the emptied rank-1 slot: a wrong-type or step-shuffled exemplar (the program already has blind1) placed where the backfill item goes, so that F, H1, B1 and the filler arm are compared at matched set size and matched prompt length. As written, g_1 = s(B1) - s(H1) contrasts a 3-item, longer prompt against a 2-item, shorter one, so it confounds the next-ranked item's CONTENT with the mere presence of a third demonstration and a few hundred extra tokens -- and the round's own binding rules demand token- and rate-matched placebos. Note that the S1 arm is token-matched but H1 is not, so the reported ordering s(H1) < s(S1) < s(B1) is partly a length ordering. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also name: a Shapley-under-hole vs Shapley-under-backfill contrast on a subsample (the brief lists Shapley as a ground-truth estimator, and 'which reference' applies to it too, so excluding it purely on cost is weak), and a random-rank backfill (fill the slot from rank 5-7 instead of rank 4) to show the gap tracks retriever rank rather than any additional expert item.
preprint_collision: No verified collision found. My queries, all through the s2cli channel (Semantic Scholar + HuggingFace, both reported ok on every call; WebSearch unavailable in this session, WebFetch not used): (a) 'counterfactual reference baseline for removing a retrieved item: empty slot versus next-ranked replacement' --recent -> 7 hits, nothing on the mechanism (closest was CUE-R arxiv:2604.05467, plus arxiv:2609.01865, 2608.12652, 2506.20854); (b) 'per-item credit assignment for retrieved experience memory in LLM agents leave-one-out' --recent -> 11 hits, all system papers that score memory items without validating the score against any counterfactual (AttriMem 2607.21106, MemQ 2605.08374, TreeMem 2605.04811, A-MAC 2603.04549, Memory-R2 2605.21768, MemSifter 2603.03379, LUCID 2608.00017) -- consistent with the brief's stated gap; (c) 'choice of baseline value in feature attribution changes the explanation removal versus replacement' -> returned the XAI baseline literature including arxiv:2110.11929 (deletion-based metrics are biased relative to plausible MLM-synthesized replacements) and arxiv:2412.17512 (BEE, learned baselines), i.e. the reference-choice point is long established outside RAG; (d) 'explaining by removing unified framework how features are removed baseline distribution Shapley' -> arxiv:2011.03623, the canonical statement that removal-based explanations are parameterized by how the feature is removed; (e) 'marginal value of a document equals its value over the next best alternative in a ranked retrieval list' -> EMPTY for this mechanism (12 hits, all reranking architecture papers: GroupRank 2511.11653, E^2Rank 2510.22733, JointRank 2506.22262, Rank-K 2505.14432, 2411.11767); (f) 'deleting a document from a retrieval corpus promotes the next ranked document effect on downstream accuracy' --recent -> EMPTY for the claim (5 hits on retriever position bias and distractor dose: 2605.26578, 2605.10828, 2503.05037); (g) 'CUE-R intervention based per-evidence utility remove replace duplicate retrieved evidence' -> CUE-R 2604.05467 and CoRM-RAG 2605.01302, neither using the retriever's next candidate as the reference. On the proposal's own Preprint Collision Check: it is above the median for this pipeline -- four queries, channel named, IDs attached, recency restriction used on two, and an explicit statement that WebSearch was not used -- and its characterizations of CUE-R, 2507.04480 and 2607.14271 match what I verified. Two real weaknesses. First, it verified none of the roughly fourteen arXiv IDs it leans on; I verified 2604.05467, 2507.04480, 2607.14271, 2508.14482, 2509.12765, 2605.01302 and 2605.04811, and could NOT verify 2606.29502, 2605.30712, 2606.16285, 2512.10696, 2607.22562 or 2603.05093, so a non-trivial part of its 'nobody does this' argument rests on unchecked citations. Second, the home-vocabulary query it ran ('feature attribution baseline reference value choice') missed the canonical statement of its own mechanism (arxiv:2011.03623) and never searched the framing in which 'value over the next-best alternative' is a century-old idea (opportunity cost, VCG externality, cascade displacement in ranked lists) -- and my query (e) in that vocabulary came back empty for retrieval, which is the honest result but is a search the proposal should have run itself and reported. Empty searches here are reported as empty, not as evidence of novelty.
